primary_claim: Layer-5 head-5 of the chess transformer Maia-3, previously identified as a 'knight fork detector,' is actually knight-move-specific (no effect on pawn forks) and functions as a 'knight move auditor' that scales support with the genuine threat value of a knight move and, most distinctively, harshly suppresses pointless (bad and quiet) knight moves nearly 3x more than bad attacking moves

effect.metric: mean change in logit from ablating head l5h5, by move category
effect.value: pawn K+Q fork +0.10 (unaffected); hollow attacks: queen +0.56, rook +0.13, bishop -0.01, pawn -0.11; good/bad x quiet/attacking: -0.30, -0.67, 0.78, 0.27 (pointless moves suppressed 2.93x harder than bad attacking moves)

depends_on: LzeZW9PvR6Njc9ngr's earlier posts in the Fork Around and Find Out series
contradicts_or_qualifies: revises the authors' own earlier conclusion (from part 2 of this series) that l5h5 is a general 'fork detector,' since pawn forks show the head is knight-exclusive
limitations_stated: uses the 5 million parameter Maia-3 model only due to accessibility; the 23m or 79m model may have a different ontology
the mining predicates for good/bad/quiet/attacking moves are improvable and were iteratively written, and errors here are upstream of every figure
only one skill setting (high-skill play) was used; lower-skill representations are a follow-up
the logit lens only detects features within the span of the unembedding layer, constraining results to a subspace of decodable representations
quote: Its most descriptive and distinct role, though, is that it harshly suppresses pointless moves: a knight move auditor.
